metadata.title: Quote It or Refuse.
metadata.audience: INFO 7375 reviewers; hiring managers for applied-AI / LLM engineer roles
metadata.concept: A pitch for ClaimCheck: an insurance-claims Q&A tool that answers only with a verbatim quote that code has verified, and otherwise refuses. Nothing is built yet; the film says so.
metadata.note: Coursework pitch, not a channel reel. No IN-FOR-BEAR persona, no @NikBearBrown chip, no instructor name or credit line. Narration is the local Kokoro am_onyx voice (free, no key). The script was drafted with Claude in Claude Code from the student's own choices (project, alternatives tried, what to leave out) and is the student's to approve; see SOURCES.md. This checkout has no show-tell skill; ai-explainer is used instead and the substitution is logged in FRICTIONAL.md. HONESTY: every picture of the tool is a mock-up and carries a CONSTRUCTED stamp on screen; no Claude response is shown anywhere; the only past-tense evidence is Dovetail's real test output, captured and dated at build time.

beats.narration_text: A claims examiner asks one question all day: is this covered, and which clause says so? Any chat assistant will answer fluently. My final project is a tool that has to prove its answer, or refuse. I'm Shreyash Yadav, and nothing in this pitch is built yet.

beats.narration_text: ClaimCheck is a citation checker for insurance claim files. It answers only when code can verify the clause it quotes. Otherwise it says: not in the documents.

beats.narration_text: Here's the problem. A policy runs dozens of pages, and an endorsement can quietly override the base form. An answer that cites a section looks exactly like a correct one. Nobody checks whether that section exists, or whether it says what the answer claims.

show.at: Nobody checks whether that section exists

Small stamp lower-left: CONSTRUCTED EXAMPLE - synthetic text.

beats.narration_text: So here is what I will build: a public GitHub repository holding a Python command-line tool on Claude, with its test set and eval report. Claude must return an answer, a word-for-word quote, and the document it came from. Then plain code checks two things. Does the quote exist in that document? Does it contain the answer? Fail either, and the answer never reaches the reader.

beats.narration_text: This is the prompt contract, and it is still a proposal. The model either fills all four fields, or sets the status to not in documents. A parser enforces the format, so a reply that drifts from the contract fails as loudly as a wrong answer.

beats.confirmed: 2026-10-07: student confirmed trying both alternatives (chat assistant + PDF upload; LlamaIndex/LangChain RAG). No third alternative.
beats.narration_text: I looked at two things people already use. Uploading the PDF to a chat assistant gives a fluent answer, but nothing checks the citation, and there is no test set. A LlamaIndex or LangChain RAG template retrieves good chunks, but out of the box it returns whatever the model says. ClaimCheck will save a claims examiner from acting on a cited clause that nobody checked, which neither of those does.

beats.narration_text: Who opens it? A hiring manager for an applied AI engineering role at an insurtech or health tech company. In the first minute, they read the README, run one command, and get this report, with failures listed first next to the clause the tool cited. This table is a mock-up. There are no results yet.

beats.narration_text: If it works, a reviewer could fairly conclude one thing: I can put a checker around a language model and measure it honestly. Each skill maps to a file they can open. What they could not conclude is that it works on real claims. It will only ever see synthetic data.

shot.visual_intent: Four skill labels on the left, each wired to the file that will prove it on the right; a boundary line below.

Chip under the line: 'synthetic data only'.

beats.narration_text: The scope. In: one synthetic claim file and thirty to fifty questions, at least a third of them traps. Out, on purpose: it will never decide whether a claim is covered. It finds and quotes; a person decides. First to run: one policy, ten questions, and the checker. You'll know it ran when a dated report exists.

beats.confirmed: 2026-10-07: no classmate blind questions arranged; mitigation list left at three items.
beats.narration_text: What could sink it: I write the documents, the questions, and the tool. So the test can end up measuring my own blind spots, and the score looks better than it is. My answer: freeze the test set before I tune any prompt, make a third of it adversarial, and log every prompt change next to its score.

shot.visual_intent: A closed loop of 'me' writing every part, then three mitigations break the loop.

One third of the questions node turns terracotta: 'adversarial'.
A log strip unrolls: 'prompt v1 -> score', 'prompt v2 -> score'. Gauge settles back toward the dashed mark.

beats.confirmed: 2026-10-07 21:41-21:42 EDT (evidence file stamped 21:42): `pytest -q` in the Dovetail repo -> 47 passed (Python 3.13.14). Full output: evidence/dovetail-pytest-2026-10-07.txt. Cybersenz deliberately not mentioned (student's choice).
beats.narration_text: Why this project? It's a mix. Wrapping a model in a deterministic checker is something I have done before. In Dovetail, my errand-planning agent, a solver checks the model's plan, and all forty-seven of its offline tests passed when I re-ran them on October seventh. The Claude API, prompt contracts, and a source-grounded test set are new to me. And insurance is the domain I want to work in.

Footer chip: 'target domain: insurance / health tech'.

beats.narration_text: So, honestly: today this project is a brief, a beat sheet, and this film. Everything else is will. The synthetic claim file, the frozen test set, the tool and its checker, and a report that lists its own failures first.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude with any long document you have the right to share. Here is a document. Answer my question only with a word-for-word quote from it. If no sentence answers it, reply exactly: not in the document. Then search for that quote yourself. That manual check is the step ClaimCheck will automate.
